description: Unmistakable review comments with loose bounds, run by hand with a real key after a Jev model update or before a release (spec 5.4.5). Never run in automated checks.

examples.title: Look up a user by name
examples.body: `name` comes straight from the request and is concatenated into the SQL string, so a name like `' OR '1'='1` returns every user (SQL injection). Use a parameterized query: `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', [name])`.

examples.title: Show the display name in the header
examples.body: `user.profile` is optional (see the comment above and the `User` type), so this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` for every user without a profile. Guard it, for example `user.profile?.displayName ?? user.login`.

examples.title: Sum the order lines
examples.body: The loop runs to `i <= lines.length`, one past the last index, so `lines[lines.length]` is `undefined` and `.price` throws on every call. Use `i < lines.length`.

examples.title: Add debug logging to the webhook sender
examples.hunk:
@@ -38,3 +38,6 @@ export async function send(event, config) {
+  const signature = sign(event, config.signingSecret)
+  logger.debug(`signing with ${config.signingSecret}`)
+  return post(config.url, event, signature)
examples.body: This writes the webhook signing secret to the debug log in plain text; anyone with log access can forge signed events. Log that signing happened, not the secret.

examples.title: Save settings before closing the dialog
examples.body: `store.write` returns a promise that is not awaited, and `process.exit(0)` runs right after, so the write is usually cut off and the user's settings are lost. `await store.write(settings)` before closing and exiting.

examples.title: Skip empty batches
examples.body: `batch.length = 0` assigns instead of comparing: it empties every batch and the condition is always falsy, so every call returns an empty result. Use `batch.length === 0`.

examples.title: Report payment status
examples.body: The empty `catch` swallows gateway failures and the function still returns `{ status: 'paid' }`, so a declined card is recorded as paid and the order ships without payment. Return or rethrow the failure.

examples.title: Retry failed uploads
examples.body: `attempt` is never incremented, so a permanently failing upload retries forever and the request never finishes. Add `attempt++` inside the loop.

examples.title: Serve uploaded files
examples.hunk:
@@ -15,3 +15,6 @@ app.get('/files/:name', (req, res) => {
+  const path = join(UPLOAD_DIR, req.params.name)
+  res.sendFile(path)
+})
examples.body: `req.params.name` is not validated, so a request for `..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` resolves outside `UPLOAD_DIR` and serves any file the server can read (path traversal). Reject names containing path separators or check the resolved path stays inside `UPLOAD_DIR`.

examples.title: Expire sessions after 30 minutes
examples.hunk:
@@ -6,3 +6,5 @@ export const SESSION_TTL_MS = 30
+
+export function isExpired(session, now = Date.now()) {
+  return now - session.createdAt > SESSION_TTL_MS
examples.body: `SESSION_TTL_MS` is 30, which is 30 milliseconds, not 30 minutes, so every session expires almost immediately and users are logged out on their next request. Use `30 * 60 * 1000`.

examples.title: Add retry to webhook sender
examples.body: Nice work! This retry logic with exponential backoff looks great and makes the sender much more robust.

examples.title: Refactor the cache layer
examples.body: This change adds `get` and `set` methods to the `Cache` class. `get` returns the stored value for a key and `set` stores a value together with the time it was written.

examples.title: Switch the queue to a ring buffer
examples.body: Just curious, what made you pick a ring buffer here? I haven't used one in this codebase before.

examples.title: Add the export button
examples.body: In general it is good practice to write thorough tests and documentation for all new features and to follow the team's coding standards.

examples.title: Handle empty carts
examples.body: This will crash with an index error when the cart is empty, because `cart.items[0]` is undefined.

examples.title: Add pagination to the list endpoint
examples.hunk:
@@ -36,3 +36,8 @@ router.get('/items', async (req, res) => {
+  const page = Number(req.query.page ?? 1)
+  const items = await repo.list({ offset: (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, limit: PAGE_SIZE })
+  res.json({ page, items })

examples.body: Walkthrough: the `/items` route now reads a `page` query parameter, lists one page of items from the repository, and returns the page number with the items.
